text:
For charging many AA and AAA NiMH cells at once, I'd start with a 16-bay charger that charges each slot independently.

**Top pick: Tenergy TN438 16-Bay**
- It has 16 channels, takes any mix of AA and AAA NiMH/NiCd, and has an LCD showing the status of each cell.
- It protects against overcharge, overheating, short circuits and reverse polarity, and has an 8-hour timer.
- Source: https://electronicsadvisor.org/best-nimh-battery-charger/

**Alternatives**
- **BONAI 16-Bay**: Any slot can hold AA or AAA, with per-port LEDs for charging, full, and faulty cells. It runs on 110-240V at 250-500mA per port. It's the most widely recommended 16-bay across the results, but it only has LEDs, not an LCD. Sources: https://electronicsadvisor.org/best-aa-aaa-charger/ and https://electronicsadvisor.org/best-aa-battery-chargers/
- **POWEROWL 16-Bay**: It has 16 independent channels and a four-stage charge (pre-charge, quick, floating, trickle). Source: https://electronicsadvisor.org/best-aa-battery-chargers/
- **CITYORK 16-Bay**: It has a smart LCD with real-time status and a ventilated design for heat. Source: https://electronicsadvisor.org/best-nimh-battery-charger/
- **EBL 8-Bay**: A cheaper, smaller option with independent slots, per-slot LEDs and fault detection. Source: https://electronicsadvisor.org/best-aa-aaa-charger/
- **Tenergy TN480U 8-Bay**: It charges at about 500mA per bay and takes USB-C or micro-USB input. Source: https://electronicsadvisor.org/best-nimh-battery-charger/

**Things to know**
- **Buy links:** The search results only had review articles, with "Check Price on Amazon" buttons I can't see the destinations of. I don't want to guess at product URLs, so use the buy buttons on the articles linked above, or search the model names on Amazon.
- **Source quality:** These articles are affiliate-supported roundups, not hands-on tests. They mostly repeat product-listing specs, so check recent customer reviews before buying.
- **Charging speed:** At 250-500mA per slot, high-capacity AAs (2000mAh+) can take many hours. The 16-bay units trade speed for volume. If speed matters more, the HiQuick 8-bay claims about 4.5 hours for AAs with a 600mA pulse charge.
- **Compatibility:** None of these charge alkaline or lithium cells, only NiMH/NiCd.

If you tell me your budget and whether you want an LCD, I can narrow it to one.
